issue.title: "Calling dict function without Dictionary: provider#stderr_collector"

repository.name: deoplete.nvim
repository.description: :stars: Dark powered asynchronous completion framework for neovim/Vim8

issue.body:
I'm running the latest version of deoplete (`ef11a667beefd172da1d3f2df201be58f6f1f33a`) and the latest version of deoplete-rust (`0a86e502113910c33448b337c4d50cabea120d25`) and recently an error has been popping up when attempting to complete rust code in the vim status bar/message log:

> Calling dict function without Dictionary: provider#stderr_collector

It happens several times a line, and it is very obstructive.

I'm not sure if this is an error in deoplete or deoplete-rust, but I did not experience this previously. I tried to enable debug logging for the rust source (`call deoplete#custom#set('rust', 'debug_enabled', 1)`) and `call deoplete#enable_logging('DEBUG', 'deoplete.log')` but the log did not contain anything useful when this error was encountered.

My config file:

```vim
call dein#add('Shougo/deoplete.nvim', {'on_i': 1})
call dein#add('sebastianmarkow/deoplete-rust', {'on_i': 1), {'on_ft': ['rust']})
call dein#set_hook('deoplete.nvim', 'hook_source', function('ConfigDeoplete'))

function! ConfigDeoplete()                                                                                                                 
    set shortmess +=c                                                                                                                      
    call deoplete#custom#set('rust', 'rank', 99999) 
    call deoplete#custom#set('rust', 'debug_enabled', 1)                                                                                   
endfunction

call system("which racer")
if v:shell_error == 0
    let g:racer_cmd = systemlist('which racer')[0]
    let g:racer_experimental_completer = 1
    "since we are using deolete-* completions, we can comment that out
    let g:deoplete#sources#rust#racer_binary = systemlist('which racer')[0]
    let g:deoplete#sources#rust#rust_source_path = $RUST_SRC_PATH
    let g:deoplete#sources#rust#documentation_max_height = 20
endif

let g:deoplete#enable_at_startup = 1
" let g:deoplete#enable_ignore_case = 1
let g:deoplete#enable_smart_case = 1
" let g:deoplete#enable_camel_case = 1
let g:deoplete#enable_refresh_always = 1
let g:deoplete#sources#rust#show_duplicates = 0
let deoplete#tag#cache_limit_size = 5000000
let g:deoplete#sources = {}
let g:deoplete#sources._ = ['buffer', 'tag']
let g:deoplete#sources.cpp = ['clang']
let g:deoplete#sources.rust = ['rust']
autocmd CmdwinEnter * let b:deoplete_sources = ['buffer']

```

body:
The commit just adds stderr report.
So the commit is not the problem.

It seems clipboard provider is broken.
I can reproduce the error by the below vimrc.

```vim
if has('unnamedplus')
  set clipboard& clipboard+=unnamedplus
else
  set clipboard& clipboard+=unnamed
endif
```

You can get the error by the text yank.

I'm sorry about the symbols; this is on a remote OS X installation and it doesn't seem possible to use gdb from the command line since it's not codesigned and you can only codesign it with UI access; so this is from lldb.

I guess I should have been clearer.  I know what the trace looks like, but since I can't reproduce it locally I'm unable to investigate what the cause of getting into that state is.

Someone who can reproduce it, and is willing to poke around in the debugger, can either use the patch to get a core or attach a debugger to their nvim and break when `error = ERROR_DICT;` is set to figure out why there is no self dictionary.
I'm ssh'd into a locked-down OS X installation where apparently gdb cannot be used. If I can get it to reproduce locally I will try to do that, though.
The error could just as well be in `callback_from_tv`

The problem is, that in `set_selfdict`, `find_func` is used. However it won't try to autoload a function not in memory. Therefore it defaults to not treating it as  a self function. However, when the function later is called it is autoloaded and then treated as a dict function. `set_selfdict` should either try to autoload the function, or default to constructing a partial with self (and then make sure `call_callback` will ignore the self attribute if the function turns out to not be dict function)
reproducible in vim (simple test case without jobs), I will send to vim-dev.

Hmm, even with the simple directions you describe on [vim-dev](https://groups.google.com/d/msg/vim_dev/I7AXOyv-P4o/DzbyOxDHBgAJ), I can't reproduce the problem...  It works fine for me with NVIM v0.2.1-647-g55c0401df.
Are you sure that the file is not autoloaded before the script runs?

Ok.  I wasn't following the exact steps from the vim-dev post (my bad) and my normal usage wasn't hitting the problem because pythonx was resolving the autoloaded function before the clipboard provider.

Thanks for root causing it, @bfredl!
So is this a regression from 0.2.0?
No, the code was broken in 0.2.0.  We just didn't happen to trip over the problem in 0.2.0.  That doesn't mean other plugins wouldn't have, though.
@jamessan thanks. That tallies with my experience, I think.

issue.title: provider: Remove dict attribute from stderr_collector

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
If an autoloaded function hasn't been resolved before it is used in
function(), the self dict will not be created which causes E725 when
calling the function.  Since self isn't being used in
provider#stderr_collector, we can remove the dict attribute to
workaround the self dict bug[0].

Closes #7115

[0]: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/vim_dev/I7AXOyv-P4o/DzbyOxDHBgAJ
